html:
On this map in 300 CE, the eastern half of the Roman Empire is shown as the domain of Diocletian, senior emperor of the Tetrarchy. It covered the Balkans, Anatolia, Syria and Egypt.

Diocletian took power in 284 after decades of civil war and invasions. He shared rule with Maximian in the West and in 293 added two junior emperors; his own was Galerius. Diocletian ruled mostly from Nicomedia in Anatolia. He doubled the number of provinces, enlarged the army, reformed taxes and, in 301, issued the Edict on Maximum Prices to fight inflation. Galerius beat the Sasanians in 298.

In 303 he began the Great Persecution of Christians, the last and harshest. In 305 he became the first emperor to retire of his own free will, to his palace at Split. His division of East and West foreshadowed the later Eastern Roman Empire.
